payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery designed to suppress electrolyte crossover, a principal aging mechanism. An independent audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee, retracting the earlier 12,000-cycle claim. The cell’s confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. At projected 500 MWh manufacturing scale, its stack-level cost is $61/kWh. The chemistry cannot operate below 4 °C because the thalliline dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte.

payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover and improve longevity in grid storage. An independent teardown audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee, retracting the earlier higher claim. The cell’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, and projected stack-level cost at 500 MWh manufacturing scale is $61/kWh. Its key limitation is a 4 °C operating-temperature floor, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
